name: dotnet-msix

Package .NET desktop apps as MSIX from a `.csproj` (Windows App SDK 1.6+, .NET 8+, Windows 10 build 19041+) or WAP project. Windows 10 build 1709+ supports App Installer auto-update. Covers signing, Store submission, sideloading, enterprise deployment, updates, bundles, CI/CD.

WinUI 3 setup and MSIX vs unpackaged: [skill:dotnet-winui]. Native AOT: [skill:dotnet-native-aot]. CI/CD: [skill:dotnet-gha-patterns], [skill:dotnet-ado-patterns]. NuGet: [skill:dotnet-nuget-authoring]. Containers: [skill:dotnet-containers].

WinUI 3/Windows App SDK apps can package directly from `.csproj`; WPF/WinForms apps use a Visual Studio “Windows Application Packaging Project” (`.wapproj`) referencing the app project. Set manifest identity, capabilities, and assets. MSIX bundles support multi-architecture.

Build:
dotnet publish --configuration Release --runtime win-x64 \

All MSIX packages must be signed to install on Windows. The signing certificate's Subject must match the `Publisher` attribute in the package manifest.

Development self-signed certificate:
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate `
-Subject "CN=My Company, O=My Company, L=Seattle, S=WA, C=US" `
-FriendlyName "MyApp Dev Signing" `
-CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" `
-TextExtension @("<REDACTED_IP>={text}<REDACTED_IP>.<REDACTED_IP>.3", `
"<REDACTED_IP>={text}")
$password = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" -Force -AsPlainText
Export-PfxCertificate -Cert $cert `
-FilePath "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
$signtool = Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin\*\x64\signtool.exe" |
Sort-Object { [version]($_.Directory.Parent.Name) } -Descending |
Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
& $signtool sign /fd SHA256 /a /f "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

Production direct distribution: use a trusted CA; Subject must match the `Publisher` in `Package.appxmanifest`; timestamp signatures for long-term validity.
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /sha1 "THUMBPRINT_HERE" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /f "production-cert.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

Store apps are re-signed by Microsoft; no production signing certificate is needed for Store-only distribution. Register at https://partner.microsoft.com/dashboard, reserve the app name, build with Store association, then submit `.msixupload` through Partner Center.
dotnet publish --configuration Release --runtime win-x64 \

Signing options: development—self-signed (install cert manually); enterprise—self-signed/internal CA (deploy cert via Group Policy); direct download—trusted CA; Store—test cert, re-signed by Microsoft.

App Installer (`.appinstaller`) supports sideloading and auto-updates; host files on a web server, network share, or CDN. Users install via:
ms-appinstaller:?source=https://mycompany.com/apps/MyApp.appinstaller

Enterprise deployment: Intune, SCCM/MECM, Group Policy/DISM/PowerShell.
Add-AppxPackage -Path "\\fileserver\apps\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
Add-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online `
-PackagePath "MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix" `

App Installer XML controls update-check interval, prompts, activation blocking, background checks, and downgrade behavior. For custom update UI, use `Package.Current.CheckUpdateAvailabilityAsync()`. Differential updates download changed blocks when `PackageName` and `Publisher` remain the same.

See [references/detailed-examples.md](references/detailed-examples.md) for complete examples and advanced patterns.
